claims.statement: `[cognition] enabled` (shipped `false`) is the single flag governing the whole Cognition subsystem: off, the composition root builds neither the wake evaluator's session hook nor the runner, the ingest stimulus stage's wiring is `None`, so no stimulus is appended, no wake recorded and no model call made.

`[cognition] enabled = true` is refused at boot (`require_session_hook`, surfaced as `StartupError`) unless a session runner was built, the evaluator holds its hook, and at least one unit names a `home_room = true` room in `policy.toml`; config.example.toml additionally requires `[dreamer] enabled`, `[notes] enabled` and a `[dreamer.budgets.cognition]` block.

Every stimulus kind has its own producer and the evaluator claims none on their behalf: `message`/`edit`/`reaction`/`delete` from the ingest stimulus stage, `rollup` from the analytics unit rollups, `social` from the social perception poller, `self` from the session's own `wake_at` (`nora/agent/cognition_pace.py`), and `time` from the wake evaluator's floors and look-ahead; `play` is a defined kind that nothing in the tree raises.

`nora.domain.stimuli.decide` is a pure function of a `UnitView`, a `WakePolicy` and a clock that tries the wake reasons in the table's order — `settled`, `strong_cue`, `batch`, `max_age`, `time`, `self` — and returns a `Verdict` with the reason, the claimed stimuli, the consumed range and whether it cut a cooldown; there is no `rollup` reason at all.

`settled` and `strong_cue` count observed kinds only (`message`, `social`, `play`), so a pending `time` or `self` row cannot be recorded under the room-quiet reasons, and after a `strong_cue` wake whose session actually ran only re-arming cues count as strong.

The brakes are applied in a fixed order — single-flight per unit, cooldown after each session, per-unit exponential failure backoff capped at `backoff_max_seconds`, and the cross-unit `max_concurrent_sessions` which only the evaluator can apply — and every brake is recomputed from durable rows so the evaluator is stateless between ticks and a restart changes nothing.

A strong cue may cut a cooldown exactly once (a wake that cut one leaves a cooldown nothing can cut) and never a backoff, so a unit whose sessions keep failing cannot be re-woken by a room that keeps naming a time.

Single-flight is derived from the wake rows: with a hook the unit is in flight while its newest wake is OPEN (no outcome row, younger than `session_timeout_seconds`) or its task is alive in this process; without a hook the wake is treated as a session lasting `session_seconds`, a stated shadow assumption.

What a wake claims is part of the rule, not an afterthought: `settled`, `strong_cue`, `batch` and `max_age` claim every pending stimulus, while `time` and `self` claim only their own kind plus the riding-along kinds and record the rest as `unclaimed_ids`, so the watermark range can never consume a stimulus the wake did not take; a wake's `through_stimulus_id` is never set below the watermark it read.

`RIDES_ALONG` holds `rollup`: a Rollup stimulus never starts a wake and is claimed by every wake, so a daily `time` floor is what bounds how long it waits (and with `time_floors = []` nothing does, by operator choice).

Two kinds of stimulus never wake a unit: a `waits` one (a person's reply to Nora inside `reply_quiet_seconds`, recorded and consumed like any other) and an inert kind (`time`, while no skill ships for the `time` agenda kind); both exclusions come from one place so `decide`, the pending-age gauge and the health command agree.

The watermark is the wake log itself — the `(through_stimulus_id, at_ms)` of the unit's newest wake in that mode that did not fail or expire, plus the ids that wake left `unclaimed` — and a stimulus is consumed exactly when `id <= through_stimulus_id AND pending_since <= through_ms` (with `pending_since` = `coalesce(due_ms, recorded_at)`) and its id is not unclaimed; pending is the negation, i.e. a disjunction, so an older id that only becomes due after that wake's time bound (a `self` stimulus appended at 15:00 and due at 19:40) stays pending and is taken by a later wake. Both bounds only ever grow, which is what lets one row carry the watermark.

A tracked wake has at most one `cognition_wake_outcome` row and four fates — OPEN, CLOSED, FAILED (`failed`/`timeout`/`cancelled`) and EXPIRED (no outcome past `session_timeout_seconds`, read exactly as FAILED) — and only `closed` advances the watermark; a failed or expired wake's stimuli return to pending and the mark falls back to the newest wake beneath it that did not fail.

The two writes that decide a wake's fate (`record_wake` with a `WakeGuard`, and `record_outcome`) serialize on one transaction-scoped advisory lock per unit; without it they write-skew under READ COMMITTED (a guard sees no outcome while a close sees no later wake, and both commit).

An outcome is first-write-wins per wake, and a `closed` outcome for a wake a later wake already superseded is refused and written `timeout` with no carries, so an expired session finishing late cannot close over stimuli another session took; a closed outcome and its carry rows land in one transaction.

The evaluator's pending read lags the clock by `settle_seconds` (default twice `store_timeout_seconds`) and the wake's `at_ms` is that cutoff, because ids are assigned at INSERT and become visible at COMMIT: a stimulus recorded after the cutoff stays pending whatever its id.

The evaluator itself raises the two daily `time` floors (07:00 and 00:00 in `[cognition] timezone` by default) only while they are no more than `floor_grace_seconds` late and only once per unit per day, and with each floor raises one room-bound `upcoming` stimulus per room holding an event starting within `upcoming_days`.

`floors_ready` (whether a skill ships for the `time` agenda kind) gates the floor two ways: a unit whose wakes start sessions raises no floor, and any `time` stimulus already pending is inert — pending, never waking the unit and never claimed by a wake, so it acts as soon as the kind is ready.

One unit's failure is contained: a unit whose read or write fails is skipped this tick and counted `nora_errors_total{stage="cognition_wake"}` while the others still run, and since the watermark is only ever a written row a failure never moves it; a hook that raises while being called is logged and contained so it cannot abort the units after it.

At `max_consecutive_failures` consecutive agenda-caused failures the evaluator retracts (`stimulus_retraction`, reason `failed`) exactly the stimuli the newest agenda-failed wake claimed — never one that arrived since, and never one only an infrastructure failure claimed — so an agenda that always fails stops.

`WakeEvaluator.reclaim_orphans` runs at boot before the first tick and releases every tracked wake a previous process left open as `cancelled` with a restart detail: `cancelled` is skipped by the watermark (its stimuli are pending again) and neither counts toward the failure streak nor resets it, so a restart is never a strike and never a backoff doubling.

The situation and agenda are built once per session by pure code from the stimuli the wake claimed — one item per `(kind, room, item)` and one per room for `message`/`social`/`play`, summary text that is a count and never a conclusion, deterministic surprise ordering with ties broken by the oldest stimulus id — and capped at `max_items`, with the overflow returned separately as `deferred_stimulus_ids` so the caller's watermark excludes what the session never saw.

Every agenda item binds one room: a `message` binds the room it came from, a `social` read a room of the unit that may show it, an `upcoming` `time` item the room of its event, and every other kind the unit's home room — which is why `build_situation` takes `home_room` as a required argument.

Grounding hands each item, once per session, the Record rows that raised its stimuli (author, room, id, time, photo content) and the Register index lines it might duplicate or contradict — index lines, never bodies, and no Standing body ever pushed — and the grounder RAISES when it cannot read, so the wake is recorded `failed` and its stimuli stay pending rather than running a session on bare counts.

Grounding's boundaries are applied inside the read: only rooms of the unit, the row joined to the stimulus's own room, platform-deleted rows absent rather than withheld, lineage enforced on every pushed note and event line per `[lineage] mode` (`shadow` reporting without removing), and names resolved at read time and never serialized into the append-only session row.

A Rollup stimulus a session cannot read is not an agenda item: a `malformed` ref (one that never parses) is consumed, while a `roster_miss` (a person the roster does not know yet) is retained as a `waits` carry row so it is never consumed unseen and becomes an item again in the first session after the roster knows them.

The session's read surface is an explicit allowlist: `COGNITION_READ_CATALOGUE` intersected with the registry's read-only set, less tools withheld by an off flag or by the registry itself, built through the same `RegistryToolSource` and `cognition_grant()` the tag path uses; `_guarded_read_tools` refuses any tool not on the passed `read_only_tools` and any tool whose name shadows a session verb.

An agenda spanning several rooms gets ONE tool per read name that takes a `room` argument routed through that room's own binding, refusing a room value not on the agenda; the unit (not the room) remains the read boundary, so `record_query scope="all_rooms"` and `search_memory_workspace` may still reach the unit's other rooms.

What a session may write is exactly `SESSION_VERB_NAMES` — `close`, four `note_*`, three `memo_*`, three `event_*`, `standing_revise`, three `wake_*` and three reminder verbs — each declared with named typed parameters and a docstring, each running the validator the tag path runs, and each committing through the tier's live store stamped `established_by = cognition:<unit>` so provenance is never a model argument.

Each write verb reuses its tier's existing validator and guards rather than a second implementation: `parse_note_body` and duplicate-title checks for notes, `parse_memo_body`/`title_carries_value`/`dream_screen.offence` for memos, the event tier's `FieldMeta` field modes and `check_citations` for events, `nora.infra.sql.standing_revise` with the read base revision for Standing, `cognition_pace` caps for `wake_*`, and `check_remind` with the tag tool's `ReminderCaps` for reminders.

A verb never raises to the model: any store or seam failure inside a verb is logged with its traceback and answered `unavailable` with text that names no exception, and every refusal or unavailability is counted once by `nora_cognition_refused_total{verb,rule}` so no verb and no early return escapes the count.

A `close(written)` is measured against a write that actually landed in this session for that item (or an untagged write in a room holding the only item), never against the model's assertion; `close` is also the only verb that can end the loop early, and only when every item closed `no_change` or `covered` and no other verb was called.

The session's only ceilings are rounds, total tokens, output tokens and a wall clock, taken from `[dreamer.budgets.cognition]` and converted by `cognition_budget`; there is no per-tool, memory or pass-wide call ceiling (DEC-247) and a config that sets one is refused rather than silently dropped.

Strands returns normally when a loop is cut off at a bound, so the runner checks `stop_reason` against `LIMIT_STOP_REASONS` and raises `SessionLimitError`: the session is recorded `failed` with cause `infra`, gets no close, no strike and no carry, its stimuli stay pending and the failure backoff applies.

The session's wall clock is enforced by cancelling the model loop (`SessionTimeoutError`, recorded `timeout`), and the constructor refuses a budget whose timeout does not end at least `SESSION_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_SECONDS` (60 s) before `[cognition] session_timeout_seconds`, because a session outliving its wake would try to close into a range a later wake may hold; a unit with no home room is likewise refused at construction.

An agenda with no items is no session: `on_wake` records the wake `closed` with an "empty agenda" detail and returns before building any tool or touching the agent runner, and since the single model call site in the runner is the one `await self._agent_runner.run(...)` inside `_run_session`, an empty agenda makes zero model calls by control flow rather than by a flag.

When the loop returns, `_settle` closes every item the model left open as `waiting` with a strike (code's own close, counted `unclosed`) and `close_or_strike` escalates to `struck` at `max_strikes`; the stimuli of waiting or struck items and the ones deferred past `max_items` are RETURNED as carry rows that land in the same transaction as the wake's `closed` outcome, so a session is either closed with its carries or not closed at all.

A strike belongs to an ITEM, not a stimulus: the strike is part of the agenda grouping key, so a returning item keeps its own count while a fresh stimulus of the same room never inherits a strike it did not earn.

Failure cause is classified in one place: `agenda` only for an `AgendaError`, `infra` for everything else including anything unclassified (fail closed on the side that keeps the message), and only `prove_overflow_is_the_agenda` may turn a context overflow into an `AgendaError` — it must carry no transport evidence, have a prompt at least `overflow_window_fraction` of a KNOWN window, and repeat on the same agenda. Only agenda failures feed the strike.

Every path out of `on_wake` writes exactly one outcome keyed by the wake — a session that failed, timed out or was cancelled RAISES after recording rather than returning a normal result — and a cancelled exit is shielded from a second cancel so a shutdown (or the evaluator's `cancel_in_flight`) cannot interrupt the write.

Shutdown is ordered: `CognitionShutdown` first gives running sessions `SESSION_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS` to finish on their own, then cancels them, then lets the runner finish its outcome writes; the wake loop is already stopped by then so no new wake starts.

An architecture test pins the wake evaluator's `nora` imports to exactly `{nora.domain.ports, nora.domain.stimuli}`, so the evaluator cannot reach the session, agent, fire path or any adapter; the only connection is the typed `WakeHook` slot handed to its constructor and awaited in a background task, which the composition root fills whenever `[cognition] enabled`.

`tests/contract/test_stimulus_session_lifecycle_contract.py` binds both `StimulusStore` implementations (SQL over real Postgres and the in-memory double) to one rule set for the wake's fate: the watermark, the four outcomes, first-write-wins, the guarded wake write, superseded closes, carries riding only a `closed` outcome, retraction and the failure streak.

`CognitionSessionRunner.probe` is the evaluation seam: it builds the same tools, holds the same instruction and calls the same agent runner as a wake's session over one hand-written agenda item, with no wake, no outcome, no carry and no fired self-wake.

The loop's observable signals are named in one vocabulary: `nora_stimulus_total{kind,cue}`, `nora_stimulus_pending_age_seconds{unit}` (eligible stimuli only, 0 when none, absent until the first tick), `nora_cognition_wake_total{reason,mode}`, `nora_cognition_wake_deferred_total{brake}` with brakes `single_flight`/`cooldown`/`backoff`/`concurrency`, `nora_cognition_session_total`/`_ended_total{outcome}`/`_skipped_total{reason}`/`_limit_total{limit}`, `nora_cognition_item_total{kind,outcome}`, `nora_cognition_carry_total{state}`, `nora_cognition_stimuli_struck_total`, `nora_cognition_wake_reclaimed_total` and `nora_errors_total{stage}`.

`StimulusStore.view` answers the pending predicate as three disjoint range reads — `id > through_id` on `idx_stimulus_unit_id`, `id <= through_id AND due_ms > through_ms` on `idx_stimulus_unit_due`, and `id <= through_id AND due_ms IS NULL AND recorded_at > through_ms` on `idx_stimulus_unit_undated_recorded` — each under the due cutoff `coalesce(due_ms, recorded_at) <= now_ms` and the one live-stimulus predicate that no `stimulus_retraction` row exists, unioned with `UNION ALL` so nothing is deduplicated; `tests/infra/test_stimulus_store_plan.py` holds the plan to those three indexes because the single negated predicate would walk an append-only unit's whole history.

After the range read, `view` merges two side doors — the stimuli a `closed` session carried (its current `carried` carry rows, delivered `waits` when a person's wait closed the item) and the ids the watermark's wake left `unclaimed`, which stay pending rather than consumed — then sorts by id oldest first and truncates to the one shared `limit` (the evaluator's `pending_limit`, `DEFAULT_PENDING_LIMIT` = 1000, a different bound from the agenda's `max_items`); oldest-first plus a wake's `through_stimulus_id` being the highest id it claimed is what leaves the cut stimuli pending, both stores return the same bounded list, and `decide` carries the watermark's unclaimed ids into the next wake whether or not a truncated read showed them.
